angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 696,709 km at 121.15 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.2540 +/- 0.0203 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 121.15 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.00145 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4511 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 696,709 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.903 (0.863 to 0.943) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5418.77 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4511 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4511 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4511.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.392, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, BD+14 546: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4511 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.01811, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 30392773430255360, flags_flame 00: age_flame 10.742181 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 9.383491 to 12.100871)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
